issues.legal_issue: A claim that property has been deprived through the levy or collection of tax cannot be enforced as a fundamental right through a petition for constitutional relief.
material_facts: Tax assessments were made against the petitioner, and recovery proceedings led to attachment of his property and the sale of one property.
The petitioner sought relief under Article 32, alleging that the attachment and sale violated his fundamental rights under Articles 31(1) and 19(1)(f).
issues.conclusion: Article 31(1) concerns deprivation of property otherwise than by the imposition or collection of tax, while the right under Article 265 is not a Part III fundamental right enforceable under Article 32; the petition was therefore not maintainable in this situation.
issues.legal_principle: Under Articles 31(1) and 265 of the Constitution, Article 31(1) is concerned with deprivation of property otherwise than by the imposition or collection of tax. The right under Article 265—that tax may be levied or collected only by authority of law—is not a fundamental right conferred by Part III and cannot be enforced under Article 32. The Court followed Ramjilal v. Income-tax Officer, Mohindergarh and referred to Suraj Mal Mohta and Co. v. A. V. Visvanatha Sastri.

predicates.constitutional_writ_petition: A person brings a petition seeking constitutional relief to enforce alleged fundamental rights.
predicates.tax_collection_property_deprivation: Property is attached, sold, or otherwise taken in proceedings to recover tax.

issues.definition: When a constitutional writ petition seeks to enforce fundamental rights against property deprivation through tax recovery, the tax-collection claim is not enforceable as a fundamental right.

issues.legal_issue: The Court may decline to issue discretionary writs where the challenged proceedings have concluded and assessment orders have already been made before the petition is filed.
material_facts: The investigation proceedings had concluded more than two years before the petition was filed.
Assessment orders had been made before the petition was filed.
The petitioner sought to quash the assessment orders and restrain further interference with his property.
issues.conclusion: Even apart from the petition's lack of maintainability, the Court considered it not just and proper to issue any of the discretionary writs sought in the circumstances.
issues.legal_principle: The issue of the requested writs was discretionary, and the Court relied on the circumstances that the investigation proceedings had concluded well before the petition and that assessment orders had already been made. The Court gave this as an independent reason for declining relief; it cited no separate earlier case for this discretionary conclusion.

predicates.constitutional_writ_petition: A person brings a petition seeking a writ from a constitutional court.
predicates.challenged_proceedings_concluded_before_: The proceedings challenged in the petition had ended before the petition was filed.
predicates.assessment_orders_already_made: Tax assessment orders had been made before the petition was filed.

issues.definition: When a constitutional writ petition challenges proceedings that ended before filing and assessment orders have already been made, discretionary writ relief may be declined.
